topics.topic: Source or derivation rule for attempt_number across record_change variants
questions: Must attempt_number come from the change as given, or must record_change derive it from the existing NodeExecution count?
How can a NodeExecution's attempt_number come from the change as given when the NodeExecutionDraft carried by these changes has no attempt_number field?
How can the EffectAttempt's attempt_number come from RecordAttemptInFlightChange as given when that change has no attempt_number field?
How can the EffectApproval's attempt_number come from RequestApprovalChange as given when that change has no attempt_number field?
Must attempt_number come from the change as given, or must record_change calculate it from the existing NodeExecution count for these variants?
Must attempt_number come from the change as given, or must record_change compute it from list_node_execution_rows_by_element?

quotes: The module alone assigns, inside the transaction: store positions; the random identities trial_execution_id, binding_id, run_id, approval_id and grant_id, drawn from a cryptographically secure source and drawn again on a collision, which is a drawn identity for which the row's load operation finds a row; and every by-field (issued_by, created_by, submitted_by, added_by, activated_by, executed_by, proposed_by, accepted_by, authored_by, started_by, cancelled_by, resumed_by, released_by, decided_by, granted_by, revoked_by, resolved_by) from the actor argument; and each status the field-assignment note of a variant says it writes or sets (proposed, accepted, requested, approved, refused, active, revoked, in_flight and the rest); every other field, times and attempt_number included, comes from the change as given — an attempt_number being the element's next number as the caller read it, the one it spooled under.

attempt_number of a NodeExecution written by RecordRunProgressChange, RecordReadOutcomeChange, RecordOperationFailureChange or DecideApprovalChange, and of an EffectAttempt written by RecordAttemptInFlightChange, is one more than the number of NodeExecutions the element already has, the length of list_node_execution_rows_by_element for its ElementKey, and RequestApprovalChange gives the EffectApproval it writes that same next number as its attempt_number without writing a NodeExecution; RecordRunProgressChange writes its executions in (node_id, map_index) order with an absent map_index before index 0.
judgement.why: The first passage says attempt_number comes from the change as given, while the second requires record_change to derive it from the existing NodeExecution count for the listed variants.

topics.topic: Behavior when recording an existing StoredValue identity
questions: Must an existing StoredValue identity raise StoreInternalError because StoredValue is immutable, or is it the stated exception that returns the existing record?

judgement.why: This asks the same unchanged question as P1 about the explicit StoredValue exception to the general immutable-identity failure rule.

precedent.topic: Whether existing StoredValue records must be rewritten
quotes: A StoredValue whose value_id already exists is not written again and the existing record is returned in its place, since equal values share one identity; spooled files must already be published in the run's spool by spool_file before the change that writes their SpooledFile records.

Any other broken invariant (a linked record missing, an identity already present for an immutable record, a status change from a status the change does not start from) or a failed transaction raises StoreInternalError with nothing written.
precedent.why: The specific StoredValue rule requires returning the existing record without rewriting it, while the phrase “Any other broken invariant” excludes that stated special case.

topics.topic: Multipart handling when a file-carriage input port has no media_type
questions: Must file-carriage input ports be required to have a non-None media_type, or must the multipart rule specify how to construct the required Content-Type header and DescribedPart.media_type when the port's media_type is None?

judgement.why: This asks the same question as P2 about multipart handling when a file-carriage input port has no media_type, and the relevant texts have not changed.

precedent.topic: Required handling when a multipart file port has no media_type
quotes: prepare_request: [BEHAVIOR] For POST, PUT and PATCH without a file input the inputs not used in the path form one JSON object keyed by port name, sent as its RFC 8785 canonical bytes with content type application/json; with a file input the body is multipart/form-data with one part per input not used in the path in port name order, one part per file in list order for a many file port, each part having exactly the two headers Content-Disposition form-data with name set to the port, plus filename set to the port for a file part, and Content-Type, the port's media type for a file part and application/json without parameters for a value part whose content is the canonical JSON bytes.

prepare_request: [VALIDATION_ERROR] An input is not placeable, giving input_not_placeable with the port named, when a placeholder value is not a non-null string or integer, or a GET or DELETE query value is not a string, integer, number, boolean, null or list of those; inputs are examined in port name order and a list's elements in list order, and the first that cannot be placed is named; an input placed in the path is placed nowhere else.

Port fields (exact, no others exist): name: str, direction: PortDirection, value_schema: str, carriage: Carriage, media_type: str | None, cardinality: Cardinality, disclosure_class: DisclosureClass | None
precedent.why: The model permits a missing media type, while multipart file parts require that value and the specified placement failures do not say how this case ends.

topics.topic: Final run status when an execution is refused_by_owner
questions: Must a run containing a refused_by_owner execution end as refused, or as failed under the otherwise rule?
Must a run containing a refused_by_owner execution end with status refused or, because that execution is neither succeeded nor skipped_by_guard, with status failed?

judgement.why: This asks the same question on unchanged text as P14.

precedent.topic: Final run status when execution is refused_by_owner
quotes: If any NodeExecution of the run is refused_by_owner it reaches nothing and ends the run refused.
precedent.why: The terminal status is explicitly refused.

topics.topic: Whether size or token refusals must leave the body unread with a null id or may parse it to recover the id
questions: Must the body be parsed for its id before returning size or token refusals, or must those pre-body refusals always use a null id?
For a size or token refusal, must the body remain unread and the response id be null, or may the body be parsed to recover its id?
For a size or token failure, must answer_request avoid reading the body as required by the first passage, or read and parse it to copy a valid string or integer id as required by the second passage?

judgement.why: This asks the same question as P15 on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Whether to read a refused request body to recover the response id or leave it unread and use null
quotes: The body is one JSON-RPC 2.0 message, read only after the size and token checks.
The id of every response is the body's id member when the body is one JSON object whose id is a string or an integer, and null otherwise; reading it checks nothing and decides nothing.
precedent.why: The body is not read before size and token checks, so refusals at those checks cannot recover its id and use null.

topics.topic: Whether protected information in an arbitrary exception reason must be omitted or written unchanged
questions: For an arbitrary exception whose own reason contains protected information, must that reason be written unchanged or must the protected information be omitted?

quotes: the first step that raises — InstallationRejectedError, RefusedError from the instance check, a store refusal, SandboxUnavailableError, StopRequiredError or any other exception — stops the sequence there and propagates unchanged to the caller, the same exception with its own reason;

When run_start_sequence raises, which has already written the failing step's name, MUST write the exception's reason to standard error, without any token, credential value, configuration content or stack trace, open no entrance and return a non-zero exit code;
judgement.why: For an arbitrary exception whose reason contains protected information, writing its own reason and excluding that information cannot both be satisfied.
